exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions: Retract scapulae, plant feet flat, lower bar to mid-chest with elbows at ~45 degrees, then press to full lockout.

variations.name: Tempo Bench Press (3-1-1-0)
variations.description: 3-second eccentric, 1-second pause on chest, explosive concentric. Increases time under tension and eliminates momentum.

variations.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
variations.description: Hands placed shoulder-width apart shifting emphasis to the triceps and inner chest fibers.

variations.name: Paused Bench Press
variations.description: 2-3 second dead stop on the chest eliminates the stretch reflex, building raw pressing strength off the chest.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: Set bench to 30-45 degrees, press dumbbells from shoulder level to full extension while keeping a slight arch and shoulder blades pinched.

variations.name: Single-Arm Incline Press
variations.description: Press one dumbbell at a time to challenge anti-rotation stability through the core and correct side-to-side imbalances.

variations.name: Incline Squeeze Press
variations.description: Press dumbbells together in a neutral grip throughout the movement, maintaining constant adduction tension on the upper pecs.

variations.name: Low-Incline Press (15-degree)
variations.description: Reduced incline angle biases the clavicular head while allowing heavier loads compared to a steep incline.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.instructions: With a slight bend in the elbows, lower dumbbells in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across the chest, then squeeze back to the top.

variations.name: Tempo Fly (4-0-1-2)
variations.description: 4-second eccentric with a 2-second squeeze at the top maximizes mechanical tension through the full range of motion.

variations.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
variations.description: Performed on a 30-degree incline to target the upper chest fibers with a deep stretch at the bottom.

variations.name: Half-Rep Fly Burnout
variations.description: Perform full reps to failure, then continue with partial reps in the top half of the range to extend the set and maximize metabolic stress.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.instructions: Maintain a rigid plank position, lower chest to the floor with elbows tracking at 45 degrees, then press back up to full lockout.

variations.name: Deficit Push-Up
variations.description: Hands elevated on dumbbells or parallettes to increase range of motion and deepen the pec stretch at the bottom.

variations.name: Tempo Push-Up (5-2-1-0)
variations.description: 5-second lowering phase with a 2-second pause at the bottom turns a simple push-up into a brutally effective hypertrophy stimulus.

variations.name: Close-Stance Diamond Push-Up
variations.description: Hands form a diamond shape under the sternum, shifting the primary load to the triceps and inner chest.

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.instructions: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, grip the bar just outside the knees, and drive through the floor while keeping the bar tight to your body.

variations.name: Paused Deadlift (knee level)
variations.description: 3-second pause at knee height eliminates momentum and builds positional strength in the most mechanically disadvantaged part of the lift.

variations.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
variations.description: Ultra-wide grip increases range of motion and significantly raises upper back and trap demand.

variations.name: Tempo Deadlift (4-0-1-0)
variations.description: Controlled 4-second eccentric builds body awareness and reinforces proper hip hinge patterning under load.

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.instructions: Hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees, brace your core, and row the bar to your lower ribcage while driving the elbows behind you.

variations.name: Pendlay Row
variations.description: Each rep starts from a dead stop on the floor with torso parallel to the ground, emphasizing concentric power and eliminating momentum.

variations.name: Underhand Barbell Row
variations.description: Supinated grip increases bicep involvement and allows the elbows to tuck tighter, targeting the lower lats.

variations.name: Tempo Row (2-1-3-0)
variations.description: 2-second concentric with a 1-second squeeze and 3-second eccentric forces strict form and amplifies mind-muscle connection.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: Initiate by depressing and retracting the scapulae, pull chin over the bar while driving elbows down and back, then lower with control.

variations.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
variations.description: Hands placed 1.5x shoulder width apart to bias the teres major and upper lats with a greater stretch at the bottom.

variations.name: Tempo Pull-Up (1-2-4-0)
variations.description: Explosive pull with a 2-second hold at the top and a 4-second eccentric builds immense lat strength through the full range.

variations.name: Mixed-Grip Pull-Up
variations.description: One hand pronated, one supinated creates an asymmetric challenge that exposes and corrects grip and lat imbalances.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.instructions: Support yourself on a bench with one hand, row the dumbbell to your hip while keeping the torso square and avoiding rotation.

variations.name: Dead-Stop Dumbbell Row
variations.description: Return the dumbbell to the floor on each rep and pause 1 second to eliminate the stretch reflex and build concentric power.

variations.name: Meadows Row (landmine setup)
variations.description: Barbell in a landmine with a perpendicular stance creates a unique line of pull that hammers the lower lat insertion.

variations.name: Tempo Row (3-1-1-0)
variations.description: Slow 3-second eccentric with a 1-second peak squeeze ensures strict mechanics and maximal lat fiber recruitment.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.instructions: Sit upright with a slight lean, pull the handle to your lower sternum while squeezing your shoulder blades together at peak contraction.

variations.name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
variations.description: Using a wide bar attachment targets the mid-traps and rhomboids more than the lats.

variations.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
variations.description: Unilateral pulling allows for greater range of motion and rotational core engagement.

variations.name: Paused Cable Row (2-sec squeeze)
variations.description: A 2-second isometric hold at full contraction maximizes scapular retractor engagement and eliminates cheating.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.instructions: Brace core, press the bar from the front rack position straight overhead, finishing with the bar over mid-foot and biceps by the ears.

variations.name: Z-Press (seated on floor)
variations.description: Pressing while seated on the floor with legs extended removes all lower body assistance and demands extreme core stability.

variations.name: Push Press
variations.description: A slight knee dip generates leg drive to handle supramaximal loads, overloading the lockout and eccentric phases.

variations.name: Tempo Strict Press (3-1-1-0)
variations.description: 3-second eccentric with a brief pause at the shoulders forces strict mechanics and builds pressing endurance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: With a slight bend in the elbows, raise dumbbells out to the sides until arms are parallel to the floor, leading with the elbows not the hands.

variations.name: Cable Lateral Raise
variations.description: Constant cable tension throughout the range of motion eliminates the dead zone at the bottom of the dumbbell version.

variations.name: Lu Raise (Y-raise to lateral raise combo)
variations.description: Raise dumbbells to the front (Y-shape overhead), lower, then immediately lateral raise — doubling delt time under tension per rep.

variations.name: Single-Arm Leaning Lateral Raise
variations.description: Lean away from an upright holding a post to shift the resistance curve and increase tension at the bottom of the movement.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.instructions: Pull the rope to your forehead level while externally rotating the hands apart at the end, squeezing the rear delts and mid-traps.

variations.name: Paused Face Pull (3-sec hold)
variations.description: A 3-second isometric hold at full external rotation builds rotator cuff endurance and reinforces scapular health.

variations.name: Prone Incline Dumbbell Face Pull
variations.description: Lying face down on an incline bench and performing the pull with dumbbells removes all momentum and body english.

variations.name: Band Pull-Apart to Face Pull
variations.description: Combine a horizontal band pull-apart with a face pull in one smooth motion to hit both horizontal abduction and external rotation.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.instructions: Keep elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar in a smooth arc to shoulder height, and lower with control — no swinging.

variations.name: Tempo Curl (4-1-2-0)
variations.description: 4-second eccentric and 2-second concentric eliminates momentum and maximizes bicep time under tension.

variations.name: Wide-Grip Barbell Curl
variations.description: Wider grip biases the short head of the biceps, contributing more to bicep width and peak.

variations.name: Paused Curl (mid-range hold)
variations.description: 2-second pause at 90 degrees where leverage is worst builds isometric strength at the hardest point of the curl.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.instructions: Curl dumbbells with a neutral (palms-facing) grip, keeping elbows stationary and forearms moving in a straight line.

variations.name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
variations.description: Curling across the body toward the opposite shoulder emphasizes the brachialis and long head of the biceps.

variations.name: Alternating Slow-Eccentric Hammer Curl
variations.description: Alternate arms with a 5-second lowering phase to isolate each arm and maximize eccentric damage per rep.

variations.name: Kettlebell Hammer Curl
variations.description: The kettlebell's offset center of mass forces the forearm extensors and grip to work harder through the entire range.

exercises.name: Tricep Dip
exercises.instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars or a bench, lower until upper arms are parallel to the floor, then press up to full lockout keeping elbows tight.

variations.name: Weighted Dip
variations.description: Add a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between the feet to progressively overload once bodyweight becomes manageable.

variations.name: Tempo Dip (4-2-1-0)
variations.description: 4-second descent with a 2-second pause in the hole builds immense pressing strength from the most stretched position.

variations.name: Bench Dip (narrow stance)
variations.description: Feet on the floor, hands on a bench behind you — a regression that isolates the triceps with reduced bodyweight load.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.instructions: Lying on a bench, lower the bar toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows, then extend back to lockout.

variations.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
variations.description: Using dumbbells allows a neutral grip that is easier on the elbows and allows independent arm tracking.

variations.name: Incline Skull Crusher
variations.description: Performing on an incline bench increases the stretch on the long head of the triceps at the bottom for greater hypertrophy stimulus.

variations.name: Eccentric-Overload Skull Crusher
variations.description: 5-second eccentric to the forehead then press back explosively to recruit high-threshold motor units during the concentric.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.instructions: Bar on upper traps, break at hips and knees simultaneously, descend until hip crease is below the knee, then drive up through mid-foot.

variations.name: Paused Back Squat (3-sec in the hole)
variations.description: 3-second pause at the bottom eliminates the stretch reflex and develops raw strength and confidence in the deep position.

variations.name: Tempo Squat (4-0-1-0)
variations.description: 4-second descent builds eccentric strength, postural awareness, and is invaluable for grooving squat mechanics.

variations.name: Narrow-Stance Squat
variations.description: Feet hip-width with toes forward shifts emphasis to the vastus medialis (inner quad) and demands greater ankle mobility.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.instructions: Bar rests on the front delts in a clean grip, keep elbows high, sit straight down maintaining an upright torso throughout.

variations.name: Zombie Front Squat (no hands)
variations.description: Arms extended straight in front forces an extremely upright torso and punishes any forward lean immediately.

variations.name: Tempo Front Squat (3-2-1-0)
variations.description: 3-second eccentric with a 2-second pause challenges thoracic extension endurance and quad strength in the deep position.

variations.name: 1.5-Rep Front Squat
variations.description: Descend fully, come halfway up, go back down, then stand all the way up — one rep. Doubles time under tension in the hardest range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.instructions: Take a controlled step forward, lower the back knee toward the floor until both legs are at 90 degrees, then drive through the front heel to step forward.

variations.name: Reverse Lunge
variations.description: Stepping backward instead of forward reduces shear force on the front knee and is more glute-dominant.

variations.name: Deficit Lunge (front foot elevated)
variations.description: Front foot on a 2-4 inch platform increases range of motion and stretch on the quads and glutes.

variations.name: Overhead Lunge (dumbbell or kettlebell)
variations.description: Holding weight overhead while lunging demands tremendous core stability, shoulder endurance, and balance.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.instructions: Push hips back with a soft knee bend, slide the bar down the thighs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward to stand.

variations.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
variations.description: Unilateral version challenges balance and proprioception while exposing hamstring and glute asymmetries between sides.

variations.name: Snatch-Grip Romanian Deadlift
variations.description: Ultra-wide grip increases range of motion and posterior chain demand while heavily loading the upper back.

variations.name: Tempo RDL (5-0-1-0)
variations.description: 5-second eccentric creates massive time under tension for the hamstrings and reinforces a proper hip hinge pattern.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Leg Curl (prone on bench)
exercises.instructions: Lie face down on a bench with a dumbbell squeezed between your feet, curl your heels toward your glutes, then lower with control.

variations.name: Tempo Leg Curl (3-2-4-0)
variations.description: 3-second concentric, 2-second squeeze at the top, and 4-second eccentric maximizes hamstring fiber recruitment.

variations.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Curl
variations.description: Isolate one leg at a time to identify weaknesses and ensure balanced hamstring development.

variations.name: Paused Leg Curl (top hold)
variations.description: 3-second isometric hold at peak contraction trains the hamstrings in their fully shortened position, improving cramping resistance.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.instructions: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward explosively to float the bell to chest height — power comes from the hips, not the arms.

variations.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
variations.description: One-handed swing adds an anti-rotation demand through the core and challenges grip endurance.

variations.name: American Kettlebell Swing (overhead)
variations.description: Swinging the bell fully overhead increases range of motion and adds a shoulder stability component.

variations.name: Dead-Stop Swing
variations.description: Park the kettlebell on the ground between each rep, eliminating the backswing and forcing each rep to be generated from a dead start.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.instructions: Upper back on a bench, barbell across the hips, drive through your heels to full hip extension while squeezing the glutes hard at the top.

variations.name: Paused Hip Thrust (3-sec at top)
variations.description: 3-second hold at full hip extension forces maximal glute contraction and eliminates momentum-driven reps.

variations.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
variations.description: One leg extended in the air doubles the load per glute and exposes any strength asymmetries.

variations.name: Tempo Hip Thrust (2-3-1-0)
variations.description: 2-second concentric with a 3-second eccentric increases time under tension where the glutes are maximally loaded.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.instructions: Rear foot elevated on a bench, drop the back knee straight down until the front thigh is parallel, then drive up through the front heel.

variations.name: Deficit Bulgarian Split Squat
variations.description: Front foot on a 2-4 inch platform increases the range of motion and deepens the stretch on the working glute.

variations.name: Tempo Bulgarian (4-1-1-0)
variations.description: 4-second descent with a brief pause at the bottom builds single-leg stability and quad/glute endurance.

variations.name: Goblet-Hold Bulgarian Split Squat
variations.description: Holding a single dumbbell or kettlebell in a goblet position shifts the center of gravity forward, increasing core and quad demand.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, squeeze glutes to lift hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.

variations.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
variations.description: One leg extended in the air isolates each glute independently and challenges pelvic stability.

variations.name: Banded Glute Bridge
variations.description: A resistance band above the knees forces hip abduction throughout the movement, activating the gluteus medius and minimus.

variations.name: Tempo Glute Bridge (2-5-1-0)
variations.description: 2-second lift, 5-second hold at the top creates a brutal isometric challenge for the glutes.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.instructions: Forearms on the floor, body in a straight line from head to heels, brace as if bracing for a punch and hold — no sagging or piking.

variations.name: RKC Plank (maximal tension)
variations.description: Actively pull elbows toward toes and squeeze every muscle at max effort — turns a simple plank into a full-body isometric that can only be held for 10-15 seconds.

variations.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
variations.description: From a push-up plank, tap each shoulder alternately while resisting hip rotation — an anti-rotation core challenge.

variations.name: Long-Lever Plank (arms extended forward)
variations.description: Walking the forearms further in front of the shoulders dramatically increases the lever arm and core demand.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.instructions: Hang from a bar, posteriorly tilt the pelvis, and raise your legs until at least parallel to the floor — avoid swinging.

variations.name: Toes-to-Bar
variations.description: Full range of motion with toes touching the bar demands advanced hip flexor strength and thoracic mobility.

variations.name: Hanging Knee Raise (bent knee)
variations.description: Bending the knees shortens the lever arm as a regression for building foundational hanging core strength.

variations.name: Tempo Leg Raise (2-2-3-0)
variations.description: Controlled 2-second raise, 2-second hold at the top, and 3-second lower eliminates all momentum and isolates the abs.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.instructions: Kneel behind the wheel, brace your core, and roll out as far as you can control without letting your lower back hyperextend, then pull back.

variations.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
variations.description: Rolling out from a standing position is an elite-level core exercise that demands extraordinary anti-extension strength.

variations.name: Tempo Rollout (3-1-3-0)
variations.description: 3-second extension and 3-second return with a 1-second pause at full extension amplifies time under tension.

variations.name: Banded Ab Wheel Rollout
variations.description: Attach a band from a rack behind you to the wheel — the band assists at the hardest extended position, allowing fuller range of motion.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: Bar on your back or dumbbells in hand, rise onto your toes as high as possible, squeeze at the top, then lower heels below the step for a full stretch.

variations.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
variations.description: Unilateral raises with bodyweight ensure balanced calf development and allow full concentration on each side.

variations.name: Tempo Calf Raise (2-3-3-1)
variations.description: 2-second concentric, 3-second hold at the top, 3-second eccentric with a 1-second stretch at the bottom maximizes both soleus and gastroc stimulus.

variations.name: Paused Calf Raise (top and bottom)
variations.description: 2-second pause at full dorsiflexion and 2-second pause at full plantarflexion trains the calves through their complete contractile range.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: Seated with a barbell or dumbbell on the knees, rise onto the toes and squeeze — the bent-knee position isolates the soleus.

variations.name: Tempo Seated Calf Raise (3-2-3-1)
variations.description: 3-second concentric, 2-second peak squeeze, 3-second eccentric, and 1-second stretch at the bottom for maximal soleus time under tension.

variations.name: Single-Leg Seated Calf Raise
variations.description: Performing one leg at a time allows for heavier relative loading and correction of calf imbalances.

variations.name: High-Rep Seated Calf Raise (20-30 reps)
variations.description: The soleus is predominantly slow-twitch and responds well to higher rep ranges with controlled execution.

exercises.name: Rowing Intervals (Concept 2)
exercises.instructions: Drive with the legs first, then swing the body, then pull with the arms — reverse the sequence on the recovery. Maintain a 1:2 work-to-recovery ratio on the slide.

variations.name: 500m Repeats (sprint intervals)
variations.description: All-out 500m efforts with 2-3 minutes rest between sets builds anaerobic capacity and peak power output.

variations.name: Damper 10 Power Pulls
variations.description: Set the damper to max, perform 10 powerful single strokes with full resets between each pull to build rowing-specific maximal power.

variations.name: Slow-Rate Rowing (18-20 SPM)
variations.description: Low stroke rate forces you to generate more power per stroke while building aerobic base and technical efficiency.

exercises.name: Assault Runner Sprints
exercises.secondary_muscles: quadriceps, hamstrings, calves, core, hip flexors
exercises.instructions: Lean slightly forward, drive with the balls of your feet, pump your arms aggressively — the belt is self-powered so effort directly controls speed.

variations.name: 10/20 Intervals (10 sec sprint / 20 sec walk)
variations.description: Short maximal sprints with incomplete rest develop alactic power and recovery between high-intensity efforts.

variations.name: Calorie Target Sprints
variations.description: Sprint until you hit a calorie target (e.g., 15 cals) then rest — forces maximal output as calories get harder to earn at higher intensities.

variations.name: Incline Walk (hands-free)
variations.description: Steady-state walking without holding the handles builds aerobic base while challenging balance and posterior chain endurance.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.secondary_muscles: chest, shoulders, triceps, quadriceps, hip flexors, core
exercises.instructions: Drop to the floor with chest touching, push up, jump feet under your hips, and explode into a jump with full hip extension at the top.

variations.name: Burpee to Pull-Up
variations.description: Perform a standard burpee under a pull-up bar and jump into a pull-up at the top — combines pushing and pulling in one brutal movement.

variations.name: Tempo Burpee (controlled descent)
variations.description: Slow, controlled lowering to the floor with a deliberate push-up turns a chaotic movement into a controlled strength-endurance exercise.

variations.name: Lateral Burpee (over dumbbell)
variations.description: Perform the burpee then jump laterally over a dumbbell adding a frontal-plane athletic component and coordination challenge.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.instructions: Pick up heavy dumbbells or kettlebells, stand tall with shoulders packed down and back, and walk with controlled steps while maintaining a rigid torso.

variations.name: Single-Arm Suitcase Carry
variations.description: Carrying load on one side only creates a massive anti-lateral-flexion demand on the obliques and quadratus lumborum.

variations.name: Overhead Carry (waiter's walk)
variations.description: Holding a kettlebell locked out overhead challenges shoulder stability, thoracic extension, and full-body coordination under load.

variations.name: Tempo Carry (slow march)
variations.description: Deliberately slow, exaggerated steps with a brief single-leg pause each step increases time under tension and balance demand.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.instructions: From lying flat with a kettlebell locked out overhead, move through a precise sequence — roll to elbow, post to hand, bridge, sweep leg, kneel, stand — then reverse it all back down.

variations.name: Half Get-Up (floor to seated)
variations.description: Stop at the tall-sit position and reverse back down — a regression that isolates the most core-intensive portion of the movement.

variations.name: Tempo Get-Up (5-sec per transition)
variations.description: Hold each of the 7 positions for 5 seconds, turning one rep into a 70-second full-body stability and endurance challenge.

variations.name: Bottom-Up Kettlebell Get-Up
variations.description: Holding the kettlebell upside-down by the handle demands extreme grip strength and shoulder stabilizer activation throughout the entire movement.

exercises.name: Rower
exercises.instructions: Drive with the legs, then swing the torso back and pull the handle to the sternum; reverse the sequence to return.

exercises.name: Air Bike
exercises.instructions: Push and pull the handles while driving the pedals; effort scales with how hard you go.

exercises.name: Ski Erg
exercises.instructions: Hinge at the hips and drive the handles down and back, engaging lats and core each stroke.

exercises.name: Echo Bike
exercises.instructions: Fan bike with simultaneous arm and leg drive for full-body conditioning.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.instructions: Steady or interval cycling; adjust resistance and cadence for intensity.

exercises.name: Treadmill Run
exercises.instructions: Run at a set pace/incline; maintain relaxed posture and quick cadence.

exercises.name: Run
exercises.instructions: Outdoor or track running at the target distance or duration.

exercises.name: Walk
exercises.instructions: Brisk walking for recovery or zone-2 conditioning.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.instructions: Bounce on the balls of the feet, turning the rope from the wrists.

exercises.name: Stair Climber
exercises.instructions: Continuous stepping; stand tall and avoid leaning on the rails.

exercises.name: Elliptical
exercises.instructions: Low-impact striding with arm drive; adjust resistance for intensity.
